connections setting up
·IP
192.168.15.18
·Port
Sensor control
· Connection
Connect to the sensor
· Weld type
Select the weld types that need to be identified, such as butt joint, corner joint, lap joint, 
etc.
· Track precision
Low precision: When the camera processes the image, it will lose some details of the 

image. It has filtering effect and is suitable for fillet weld.
Medium Precision: The camera has slightly higher ability of recognizing details than low 
precision when processing images. The filtering effect is moderate. It is suitable for docking 
and overlapping welds.
High Precision: The camera has the highest ability to recognize the details of the weld 
seam when processing images. It can capture more and finer welds. The disadvantage is that 
it is prone to jump and has poor filtering effect. It is suitable for very fine and flat butt welds.
· Exposure
Normally,Normally set not more than 80 ,the more reflective the workpiece is, the shorter 
the exposure time is. When a very thick laser beam appears on the image, it proves that the 
exposure time is very long. The longer the exposure time, the greater the interference of arc 
light on camera imaging.
· Laser intensity
The more reflective the laser intensity of the workpiece should be smaller, the maximum 
setting is 100. When the laser beam on the image is thicker, the laser intensity should be 
reduced.
· On
Turn on the laser and you can see the picture of weld detection at the right interface.
· Track
Turn on laser tracking, and you can see the picture of seam detection on the right 
interface, as well as the seam position detected by laser tracker.
Tracking State and Sample Collection
· Capture Image 
Acquisition of static images captured by laser tracker
Sample images are saved in the Capture Catalog of the currently running folder:

9.3 Adjustment of Laser Tracking Parameters
1. In the CRP system: enter [Technical] → <Arc welding> → <laser >, as shown below

· Laser number
Represents the different laser tracking process, the lower left corner of several parameters 
may be different, for OPENLASER () to turn on laser commands, other commands can not be 
used. (Different from the laser process invoked in SEARCHLASER() and OPENLASERTRACK()).
2. Enter the communication setting, as shown below
· Laser type
Choose JunnoVision and CRNT
·IP 
The IP address is the IP address of the laser tracker.
JunnoVision: 192.168.10.##
CRNT: 192.168.0.##
·PORT
The port number is the laser tracker port number.
JunnoVision port number: 23463
CRNT Port Number: 43002
·Link timeout
Generally set to 1S, the connection fails beyond this time
·Date timeout
It means that the system will report errors if communication fails to receive and receive 
data within a period of time.
·Connect button
Click on this button and the system will connect to the laser tracker. When the 
connection is successful, the red state light in the upper right corner will turn green.
·Open the laser button
It can be used to test whether the laser connection is successful. After the connection is 
successful, clicking on the open laser button will trigger the laser tracker to turn on the laser, 
and clicking again will turn off the laser.

3. Enter the calibration interface, as shown below
· calibration mode
Incremental or absolutely options are available
· X and Z Direction
It is used to determine whether the direction of tracking is correct or not. If the direction 
is reversed in real-time tracking, the direction can be changed by this parameter.
· Front distance
Refers to the horizontal distance between the laser wire and the end of the welding wire. 
The general setting value is 2-3 mm larger than the actual value.
· Search sensitivity
When setting the sensitivity of search, the bigger the setting value is, the bigger the 
compensation value is, and the bigger the jitter is. If the jitter is large or overshoot, the 
parameter will be reduced, and if there is a lag phenomenon, the parameter will be increased.
· Search for X and Z axis ratios
It refers to the ratio of deviation value of X-Z axis, which is set to 1 in JunnoVision 
absolutely mode and 0.01 in CRNT absolutely mode.
· Real-time tracking sensitivity
When setting the sensitivity of tracking, the bigger the setting value, the bigger the 
compensation value and the bigger the jitter. If the jitter is large or overshoot, the parameter 
will be reduced, and if there is a lag phenomenon, the parameter will be increased.
· Real-time tracking of X and Z axis ratios
It refers to the ratio of deviation value of X-Z axis, which is set to 1 in average macro 
absolute mode and 0.01 in imaginary absolute mode.
4. Enter the search para of search, as shown below

· Search times
Refers to the number of seam searches in SEARCH. If the number of seam searches 
exceeds the set number, the system will alarm.
· Search interval time
Refers to the interval in the number of searches.
· Search timeout
No welds were found during the search, and the alarm will be given after a period of 
time.
· Search distance
It is used to search the distance of weld seam in incremental mode. If the distance 
exceeds the parameter setting value, it will alarm.
· Search speed
It refers to the speed at which the robot moves to the target point when it finds the weld 
in absolute mode.
· Search for Excess Deviation Distance
It is used to search the deviation range of weld seam in incremental mode. If the actual 
distance is larger than the setting value, the alarm will be given.
5. Weld description: This description corresponds to laser tracking, as shown 
below.
9.4 Calibration of Laser Tracker
9.4.1 Robot TCP Accuracy Calibration
The accuracy of TCP should be within 2 after 20-point calibration.
If one attitude is used for calibration and another attitude is used for calibration, TCP 
will affect it. If the attitude is always used for calibration, the accuracy of TCP will not affect 
much. In the program example, the test results of the effect of TCP accuracy on the actual 

effect with different attitude can be used as a reference.
9.4.2 Laser Accuracy Testing
When connecting with the CRNT laser, the search X ratio, search Z ratio, trace X ratio and 
trace Z ratio parameters of the calibration interface need to be set to 0.01.
After the laser is installed, the laser tracking calibration interface is observed, the robot 
point position is recorded, the robot point moves 1 mm, and the data change corresponding 
to the laser tracking calibration interface is 1 mm. In theory, the laser data will change as 
much distance as the robot moves in YZ direction.
Laser is installed well, keeping the calibration board parallel to the laser line, observing 
the laser tracking calibration interface, moving the robot, so that the laser moves alone in 
one direction (X or Z). The data feedback from the laser also changes in only one direction, 
and the value is the same as the position of the robot.
9.4.3 Laser safety calibration
9.4.3.1 Sensor Installation
1. The calibration board of the laser weld tracker is shown in the following figure. There 
is a weld and “reference line” on the calibration board. The intersection point of the weld 
center line and the reference line is defined as “reference point”. The calibration plate is 
fixed on the horizontal worktable to prevent the calibration plate from moving during the 
calibration process.
The 20-point method is used to precisely calibrate the TCP parameters of the welding 
torch. If it has been calibrated, this step can be skipped and the number of the calibrated tool 
can be selected on the teaching device.
2. As shown in the figure below, adjusting the robot’s posture (revolving around A and B) 
makes the axis of the welding torch perpendicular to the calibration plate. Move the welding 
wire tips into the weld seam, adjust the position and posture of the tracker installed on the 
welding torch, make the laser line perpendicular to the center line of the weld, and the length 

of the laser line on both sides of the weld is approximately equal. At the same time, adjust the 
installation position up and down, so that the laser line in the vision is near the transverse 
axis of the camera.

9.4.3.2 calibration
1. Connect the robot to the laser tracker and turn on the laser, then enter the calibration 
interface as shown in the figure below.


2. As shown in the figure below, adjusting the posture around C makes the laser line 
coincide with the reference line (the laser line must coincide with the reference line precisely, 
otherwise the calibration accuracy will be affected).
3. As shown in the figure below, without changing the posture of the robot, it moves only 
along the X, Y and Z directions, so that the welding wire tips coincide with the “reference 
points” (the welding wire tips are located in the center of the weld and pass through the 
reference lines). Click on the Robot Instructor to record point P1.

4. As shown in the figure below, without changing the posture of the robot, it moves only 
along the X, Y and Z directions, making the laser line coincide with the reference line, and 
the length of the laser line on the left side is much longer than that on the right side. The 
record is P2.
5. As shown in the figure below, without changing the attitude of the robot, it only moves 
along the X, Y and Z directions to make the laser line coincide with the reference line, and the 
length of the laser line on the right side is much longer than that on the left side. Recorded at 
point P3.

6. In the following figure, without changing the posture of the robot, move about 20 mm 
along the Z direction of the robot and X and Y directions, so that the laser line coincides with 
the reference line, and the length of the laser line on the left is equal to the length of the laser 
line on the right. The record is P4.

7. From P1 to P4, 4 points are recorded and calculated by clicking to get the relationship 
between tools and cameras.
8. Click to modify the tool coordinate value, and automatically fill the calculated tool 
coordinate ABC into the selected tool coordinate system.
9.4.4 Laser calibration test
Direction relation, the direction of calibrated tool coordinates, when the tool coordinates 
are moved manually, X + is perpendicular to the laser line, the direction is that the welding 
torch tip is towards the laser line, and Z + is away from the calibration plate.
In proportional relation, the robot moves 1 mm in YZ direction, and the feedback data 
of the laser tracker changes 1 mm. The feedback data can be observed at the laser tracking 
and calibration interface. It can also record P points in the calibration interface, observe the 
laser position of the information prompt bar, and judge the change of feedback data. Every 
time P-point is recorded, the data information of laser feedback is printed out. First P-point 
is recorded, then 1 mm is recorded in one direction for mobile robot, and then P-point is 
recorded to observe whether the data of moving direction changes to 1 mm.

Calibration relationship compensation, the results of calibration are displayed in the 
calibration interface, and laser search can be programmed. If the location of laser search 
is different from the actual location, and the difference is fixed, the calibration relationship 
compensation can be carried out. Calibration relationship compensation in the calibration 
interface, Click to modify, you can modify the XYZ value in the input box, generally only 
modify XYZ, do not need to modify ABC. The X direction is the direction from the tip of the 
torch to the laser beam, and the Y direction is parallel to the laser beam.
9.4.5 Notes for Laser Debugging
9.4.5.1 CRNT
· Incremental and absolutely switching: Select incremental or absolute in the calibration 
interface of the teaching box.
· Incremental tool coordinate system X direction is parallel to laser beam, Y direction is 
perpendicular to laser beam, Z + direction is downward; absolute tool coordinate system X 
direction is perpendicular to laser beam, Y direction is parallel to laser beam, Z + direction 
is upward. When incremental and absolute switching, it is necessary to switch to the 
corresponding tool coordinate system.
· Laser parameters: absolutely, AX2 axis adjusted to automatic tracking, incremental, AX2 
adjusted to manual tracking.
· Laser home position can be calibrated at any position in incremental mode. Home 
position can not be calibrated after calibration in absolutely mode.
· The search ratio and real-time tracking ratio in the calibration interface of the teaching 
box are both 0.01.
· Front distance: In incremental mode, it can be adjusted by itself. In absolutely mode, 
fixed to 16.
· Incremental tracking, the relationship between the robot and the laser, is determined 
by the direction of the reference and coordinate system. Absolute tracking, the relationship 
between the robot and the laser is determined by the calibration relationship.
·OPENLASER#(0) 0 refers to turning on Laser Tracking Process No. 0
·SEARCHLASER#(1) 1 refers to calling the laser No. 1 parameter
·OPENLASERTRACK#(2) 2 refers to calling the laser No. 2 parameter
9.4.5.2 JunnoVision
· Incremental and absolutely switching: Select incremental or absolutely in the 
calibration interface of the Teach Pendant.

· Incremental tool coordinate system X direction is parallel to laser beam, Y direction is 
perpendicular to laser beam, Z + direction is downward; absolute tool coordinate system X 
direction is perpendicular to laser beam, Y direction is parallel to laser beam, Z + direction 
is upward. When incremental and absolute switching, it is necessary to switch to the 
corresponding tool coordinate system. If the direction is not right in incremental tracking, 
the direction parameters of the calibration interface can be adjusted and the direction can be 
changed.
· In incremental mode, the datum point needs to be set in the X benchmark and Z 
benchmark in the calibration interface. After the robot is adjusted to the starting welding 
position, the welding wire is aligned with the weld, and the Y and Z values searched by the 
laser are obtained.
· In absolutely mode, there is no need to set a benchmark point.
· In incremental mode, the search proportion of the calibration interface of the Teach 
Pendant is the data used for the feedback of the fuzzy laser. Multiply the data received by the 
following proportion, if the search overshoot is serious, then reduce the proportion.
· In absolutely mode, the X ratio and Z ratio is 1.
· The search sensitivity and real-time tracking sensitivity adjustment principle in the 
Teach Pendant calibration interface: the sensitivity is increased when the clock is not kept, 
and the sensitivity is reduced when the overshoot is adjusted.'
· In incremental mode, adjust the search accuracy in the teaching box search parameter 
interface, the search accuracy can be adjusted appropriately, the search accuracy adjustment 
principle: similar to the positioning error, when the data fed back by the laser is less than the 

set value, the robot thinks that the search is in place. , proceed to the next step.
· In absolutely mode, there is no need to set search accuracy. When the point is found, 
the position is not accurate, the search accuracy can be set to compensate, X compensates the 
direction of the laser beam, and Z compensates the direction of the torch.
· When calibrating the point, record the P point, trigger the laser tracker to track, then 
send the coordinates to the camera, the camera returns X/Y/Z, X is the X coordinate of the 
robot, Y/Z is the camera value, after the recording is completed, the tracking is turned off.
·OPENLASER#(0) 0 refers to turning on Laser Tracking Process No. 0
·SEARCHLASER#(1) 1 refers to the type of weld that calls laser No. 1
·OPENLASERTRACK#(2) 2 refers to the type of weld that calls laser No. 2
9.5 Introduction to Directives
OPENLASER#（0）·Turn on the laser
0 represents the invoked laser tracking process number;
When the command is run, the laser is controlled to turn on and ready to run.
CLOSELASER·Turn off the laser
When the command is run, the laser is controlled to turn off the laser.
SEARCHLASER#（0） 0·Laser Search
0 represents the invoked laser tracker parameter number (CRNT), the invoked laser 
tracker weld type (Junnovision)
0 or 1 represents whether to select GP points, 0 represents not to select GP points, after 
searching for the target directly run in place. 1 represents the number saved to GP after 
searching for the target. When saving, only XYZ is saved, but ABC is not saved. The attitude of 
the target point is based on the reference point.
When the command is run, the laser search action or the search save point action are 
executed.
OPENLASERTRACK#（0）·Turn on Laser Tracking
0 represents the invoked laser tracker parameter number (CRNT), the invoked laser 
tracker weld type (Junnovision)
When the command is run, the laser is controlled to enter a continuous search state. 
The data feedback from the laser is pushed into the buffer, and the data searched before the 
buffer is taken out for operation.
CLOSELASERTRACK·Turn off laser tracking
When the command is run, the laser is controlled to stop searching.
KEEPLASERTRACK·Keep Laser Tracking
In incremental mode, when the end of the weld is tracked, the laser can not find the 
weld, so it keeps the last searched data and completes the pre-distance. This function takes 
effect automatically without writing this instruction in the program.

When the normal calibration is completed, the welding torch is nearly vertical to the 
workpiece surface and the laser beam is nearly vertical to the workpiece surface, the test 
program can accurately find the weld seam when the Y/Z direction is offset, and guide the 
robot to let the torch tip go to the center of the weld seam.
When the welding torch is not perpendicular to the workpiece surface, the laser beam 
is not perpendicular to the workpiece surface, and the A/B posture is changed, the position 
searched by the test program and the position guided by the robot are deviated. There are 
three main aspects that affect the accuracy, TCP accuracy, laser accuracy and calibration 
accuracy.

9.7.1 Laser Search-the starting point
With laser tracker as the medium, the robot runs on the search path with laser. When the 
laser finds the required seam position, the feedback signal is sent to the robot. The robot uses 
the feedback signal of laser to find the welding position.
 The function of locating the starting point is suitable for the situation where the deviation 
of the welding starting point and the subsequent trajectory are tracked by arc or laser.
